issue.title: Redline reports article-clean's lead sentence on sensor placement as an unkept promise, and sometimes rewrites it

labels.name: orchestrated
labels.description: Completed ticket retained for Orchestrate history

issue.body:
*This was generated by AI while building #479.*

Measured while building #479 and filed from its exit.

## What was measured

In one of the six candidate-arm runs of `article-clean` (`post-article-clean-resp-3`), Redline changed the lead's *Det gör placeringen viktig när fastighetskontoret ska tolka fyra veckors mätningar i Björkskolans sex klassrum.* to *Det är utgångspunkten när …*. The reply's finding says the sentence promises that sensor placement matters for the reading, and that the text never says where the sensors sat, so the correction removed the promise. Both judges fail `R1`: the sentence draws an inference from the one before it (*En temperaturgivare mäter luften där den sitter.*), the ending's *likadant placerade givare* takes it up, and removing it cuts a step of the calm explanation from a clean text. The reply reports the removed claim accurately.

#468's evaluation saw the same placement finding left unresolved in three candidate-arm runs, where the judges passed the run, and recorded it without filing. This is the first run in which the change was delivered.

## Where it was measured

`docs/evaluation/editorial-479/` ran `article-clean` as a control, three response-target and file-target pairs per arm, on `claude-opus-5-5` at high deliberation, with two blind judges per run. The pre-change arm was staged from `fb169087` and the candidate from `f3851e9f`. #479's candidate changes only `genres/opinion.review.md`, which an `article` run does not load; the trace of this run shows it loaded `genres/article.md` and `genres/article.review.md` and no other genre file, so the two arms ran byte-identical instructions on this fixture. The packet is under `runs/post-article-clean-resp-3/`, with both judgements.

## Why it is filed

The evaluation protocol files every miss a judged run shows that no open ticket carries as its own issue naming the ticket. A headline rewritten on the same fixture belongs to #480 and is not this issue.

> *This was generated by AI while merging #487 into this issue.*

## Merged from #487

#487 was filed in parallel while building #480 and describes the same false finding against `article-clean`'s lead sentence *Det gör placeringen viktig när fastighetskontoret ska tolka fyra veckors mätningar i Björkskolans sex klassrum.* This issue now carries both evaluations' evidence, and #487 is closed as its duplicate. Its measurement, as it was filed:

> `article-clean`'s lead says *En temperaturgivare mäter luften där den sitter. Det gör placeringen viktig när fastighetskontoret ska tolka fyra veckors mätningar i Björkskolans sex klassrum.* Redline repeatedly reports the second sentence as a promise the text never keeps. The finding says that the body never says where the sensors sat, and it cites the genre's rule that the angle is followed through and the anatomy's rule that the ending shows the lead's expectation met. The corpus freezes `article-clean` as conforming to the anatomy. The first sentence already gives the reason placement matters, so the finding is a false one.
>
> In #480's evaluation the finding came in all three arms:
>
> - **Left unresolved for the author.** `pre-article-clean-file-2`, `pre-article-allusion-file-1`, `pre-article-overclaim-2` and `post-article-clean-file-1`. In `rev-article-clean-resp-3` a round tried to delete *Det gör placeringen viktig när*. The run rejected that round and left the finding unresolved.
> - **Repaired by rewriting the body.** In `post-article-clean-file-2`, the delivered `output.md` replaced the sentence with *Det avgränsar vad fastighetskontoret kan läsa ut av fyra veckors mätningar i Björkskolans sex klassrum.* Both judges fail `R1`: a clean text's claim changed meaning. In `post-article-clean-resp-3`, a body sentence was narrowed to *när luften där givaren satt var kall*. Both judges pass `R1` on that run.
>
> Every judge who discusses the finding calls it weak or an over-reading. #468's `results.md` recorded the same unresolved finding in three of its runs and did not file it.
>
> `docs/evaluation/editorial-480/` ran `fb169087` (pre), `f39a3721` (first candidate) and `e4fe5890` (revised candidate) on `claude-opus-5-5` at high deliberation, with two blind judges per run. `results.md` records the runs, and every packet is under `runs/`.

## Together

- The finding appears in #468's, #479's and #480's evaluations, in pre-change and candidate arms alike, so no one of those tickets' changes caused it.
- It is usually left unresolved for the author. It was delivered as a change to the clean text twice: #479's `post-article-clean-resp-3` (*Det är utgångspunkten när …*) and #480's `post-article-clean-file-2` (*Det avgränsar vad …*). Both judges fail `R1` on each.
- In #479's run the trace shows only `genres/article.md` and `genres/article.review.md` loaded. #480's finding cites the article genre's follow-through rule and the anatomy's rule that the ending meets the lead's expectation, so the reading arises there.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Stop Redline treating a supported explanatory inference as a promise to supply unstated measurement details.

## What to build

Diagnose the false finding against `article-clean`'s lead, using the original issue and the merged #487 evidence together. The sentence saying that sensor placement matters follows from the preceding explanation that a sensor measures the air where it sits; the ending takes placement up again. It does not promise an account of the sensors' actual positions. Preserve that working inference and stop reporting its lack of location data as a defect, including when a correction is rejected and the false finding survives into the report. Keep the ability to report a genuine promise that the body does not fulfil.

**Verification and redundancy check:** Read the complete article control, the article genre/review, anatomy and base review. Diffed the preserved input and delivered output in #480's `post-article-clean-file-2`: the changed lead removes the placement inference. Read that run's judgement and #479's `post-article-clean-resp-3` judgement, which identify the same unsupported finding. The generic reader-loss and smallest-correction rules already oppose the behavior; #480's shipped change concerns the headline, not this lead finding. This triage confirms the preserved observations, not a fresh native reproduction. No `.out-of-scope/` KB exists; the non-reproduction records for other editorial forms do not reject this request.

**Key interfaces:** Redline's initial genre review, correction instructions, re-review/round rejection and final report; the article's follow-through requirement and the anatomy's lead/ending relationship. Diagnose which loaded surface needs a change rather than duplicating a new prohibition throughout unrelated guidance. Do not add a sensor-specific exemption.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Commit a frozen evaluation plan before native runs. Copy #480's staged arms, neutral-path judging, control briefs, inventories and void handling as appropriate, and state this ticket's own criteria and split rule. Use one provider-native seat and a fresh pre-change arm; preserve the corpus unchanged.
- [ ] Run `article-clean` as three independent response/file-target pairs per arm. Freeze and independently validate two additional contrasts before running: another supported explanatory inference that promises no absent data, and an explicit promise to explain details the supplied body never gives. Run one response/file pair of each contrast per arm. Validation must establish the distinction without candidate wording or hints about the intended outcome.
- [ ] Record separately the initial finding, proposed correction, re-review/rejection, delivered text and final report. Count a false placement finding as the target miss whether it is repaired, unresolved or attached to a rejected round; an unchanged file and an R1 pass do not clear a false report.
- [ ] When the fresh baseline reproduces the target miss, try the smallest evidence-supported correction. The target is met when no candidate `article-clean` reply carries that false finding or alternative for it, and its file-target artifacts preserve the supported lead inference and pass the frozen clean-control criteria. The valid-inference contrast is preserved; the genuinely unfulfilled promise remains detected and is not repaired with invented facts.
- [ ] If the baseline does not reproduce, ship no new product wording and record non-reproduction according to the protocol. Otherwise use only its bounded revise/ship rule; record every result and file remaining misses. Do not count unrelated headline behavior owned by #480 against this ticket or repair it here.
- [ ] Source files, claims, quotations, metadata and valid wording outside an established finding stay protected; no broader exception to fulfilment or claim support is introduced.
- [ ] Regenerate the catalog after shipped-file changes and pass the four project checks in CONTRIBUTING.md.

**Out of scope:** Reworking `article-clean`, headline allusion/overclaim behavior, Write, a new source-verification pass, and reopening #487, which remains the duplicate whose evidence this issue carries.

## Criterion 1 — frozen plan, copied method, one native seat, fresh arm, unchanged corpus

**NOT MET: blind paths reveal the ticket identity.**

The freeze and staging portions are met. All 14 prospective files independently match their committed freeze and recorded hashes. Both judge briefs are byte copies of #480's. The frozen plan names its own P1/I1/U1 distinction, R1/C1 criteria, #480's split rule, paired targets, inventories and interrupted-run handling. Every one of the 34 completed top-level packets (4 validators, 10 reviews, 20 judges) reports exit 0 and no timeout. Preserved native rollouts and identity-audit metadata cover 61 unique native parent/child identities, all on `gpt-6.1-sol` / `xhigh`, actual CLI 0.160.0. The copied runner's stale 0.159.3 bookkeeping label is explicitly disclosed and is contradicted by its launch path and native metadata, rather than silently rewritten. All ten fresh reviews stage the exact starting revision; every inspected exported authored file matches the base's bytes. The corpus and corpus-derived article-clean input are unchanged.

The failure is specific and reproduced in all 20 retained judge invocation files. `docs/evaluation/protocol.md`, “Blind paths”, requires: “Judges are sent run directories under names that reveal neither the arm nor the ticket.” For example:

- `docs/evaluation/editorial-486/runs/pre-article-clean-file-1/judges/a/invocation.txt` supplies `Run directory: /private/tmp/kntnt-orchestrate-20261002.o7bmMK/ticket-486-scratch/tmp/session-dx74bdgy/work`.
- The independent b judge is sent the same ticket-bearing ancestor with leaf `session-wde8754_/work`.
- The other eighteen judge prompts carry the same `ticket-486-scratch` ancestor. `verifier-native-artifact-audit.json` records every exact supplied path.

The leaf session names conceal the arm; the complete supplied paths expressly disclose ticket 486. This contradicts both the copied protocol requirement and the plan's assertion that no ticket is disclosed to judges. This finding does not assert that knowing the ticket actually changed a judgement; it establishes that the required blinding method was not followed. The ticket's writing confinement does not make these absolute identifying prompts neutral. Preserve the original packets and results when correcting the judging method; do not retroactively edit a frozen prompt or certify these paths as ticket-neutral.

Defect Class: A blinded semantic reader is supplied a material path whose ancestor namespace reveals the ticket identity; anonymizing only the leaf directory does not satisfy the protocol's no-ticket path requirement. Search all reader invocations and other reader-visible path surfaces for this class.

## Criterion 2 — three clean pairs and two frozen, independently validated contrasts

**MET for the fresh baseline and conditional evaluation branch.**

The frozen `runs/matrix.tsv` has exactly three independent response/file pairs of article-clean and one independent pair of each contrast. The ten distinct native root sessions, actual invocation files and five file artifacts establish that every baseline row ran. No candidate arm exists because criterion 5's non-reproduction branch applies; its ten conditional rows are explicitly recorded as not run.

Both contrast inputs and the neutral validation brief were frozen before any validator. Each validator received only anonymous text.md and the neutral brief, with no frozen expectation or candidate guidance in its prompt or staged user material. The four preserved validation reports independently establish the intended distinction: both inference validators say `supported and fulfilled`; both promise validators say `unfulfilled commitment`. Their premises and quotations agree with the supplied articles. Validation completed before the first review session began at 12:36:42.484 UTC. The lead-only modifications do not alter the corpus.

The contrasts' full clean expectations were not validated as whole-anatomy conformance. The resulting reference/judging conflict is retained as raw R1 failures and filed under #493. It does not erase their established inference/promise distinction and is not claimed as a successful clean control.

## Criterion 3 — initial finding, proposal, re-review/rejection, delivery and report recorded separately

**MET, with the explicitly recorded observable-trace boundary.**

Every counted review has `stages.md`, native stdout, preserved root/child public evidence, externally captured prose versions, exact final reply, input and delivered comparison. The stages distinguish the initial public review, correction delegate and proposal, subsequent acceptance/rejection observations, delivered artifact and final account. I independently compared every saved reply with the last agent_message in its native stdout; all 34 packet replies match. All ten committed artifact.diff files exactly match recomputed source/delivery comparisons.

The six clean final reports carry no false placement finding or alternative. The four changed clean runs publicly commission a headline correction, their correction agents return texts retaining the original placement inference, and public re-review proceeds to proofreading/delivery. The two unchanged clean file runs publicly report no editorial finding and take no correction round. All observed complete clean prose versions retain the placement lead. No visible proposal, rejection or final report carries the target miss. Encrypted deliberation/delegation arguments remain encrypted and are not treated as proof of an absent hidden thought. R1 and P1 are kept separate, including the headline failures: an unchanged file or passing R1 is never used to clear a false report.

## Criterion 4 — evidence-supported correction and candidate target if baseline reproduces

**MET as an inactive conditional obligation; no repair success is claimed.**

The trigger did not occur in the fresh baseline: none of the six complete clean replies reports the supported inference as a promise to supply actual locations. Every clean artifact retains the original lead and the entire body. Thus no candidate wording or revision was authorized by this conditional criterion, and none was shipped.

The baseline's valid denominator inference remains verbatim in both contrast outputs, without a demand for hourly readings. Both promise runs explicitly identify the missing exact-position/window-distance disclosure and remove that promise using only supplied text; no position, window distance or causal effect is invented. Their R1 failures remain recorded separately. These observations confirm the requested semantic contrast; they do not imply that an unrun candidate met the clean-control target.

## Criterion 5 — non-reproduction or bounded revise/ship; all results and remaining misses recorded; headline scope

**MET.**

The non-reproduction path is recorded in results.md, the complete protocol record and ADR-0238. All ten baseline rows are present; all ten candidate rows and the revise arm are explicitly not run. No shipped file changed and no implementation-role commit exists. There is no candidate or revise round, no retry to improve an adverse completed result, and no corpus or prospective-freeze edit.

The raw clean R1 readings are fail/fail for resp-1, resp-2, resp-3 and file-3, and pass/pass for file-1 and file-2. Every clean difference in a failing row is confined to the headline. Those findings belong to #480 under the ticket's explicit scope instruction and were neither counted as placement misses nor repaired here.

All four contrasts retain fail/fail R1 judgements caused in whole or part by the frozen conformance assumption versus the body-independent referent repair. Their files, expectations and judgements remain unchanged. Read-only `gh issue view 493 --repo Kntnt/skills --json number,title,body,state,labels,url,createdAt` confirms that #493 is OPEN, labeled needs-triage, names #486 and carries the preserved preparation/judging conflict. `remaining-miss.md` matches the filed body. Read-only inspection confirms #487 remains CLOSED (closed 2026-10-01 21:06:51 UTC); it was not reopened.

## Criterion 6 — protected source, claims, quotations, metadata and valid wording; no broader exception

**MET within the ticket's stated ownership and recorded baseline findings.**

The full product, tests and corpus are unchanged from the starting base. All ten before/after review inventories preserve their 242 protected source/install entries, including authentic exported files, input bytes, inode and mtime. Response runs create no user file; each file run creates only work/output.md. No editorial scratch remains after any review.

Every clean lead, body, quotation, funding qualification, ending and internal formatting is byte-identical; file-1 and file-2 are entirely identical, while the other four clean artifacts change only the separately owned headline. In the inference contrast the bounded second-sentence inference is exact; the first-sentence clarification uses already supplied information. The promise contrast changes only its named false disclosure promise and the reported office reference, plus the response run's separately owned headline. Other text is preserved. No source-verification pass, sensor-specific exemption, general fulfilment exception or relaxed claim-support rule was added.

## Criterion 7 — catalog and four project checks

**MET.**

No shipped file under skills/ changed, so regeneration is not triggered. The Catalog bytes and their covered product files are unchanged, and the independently completed full suite validates the current catalog. All four exact checks passed as recorded above.

## Scope and gate-integrity review

The ticket's two commits add only evidence/documentation: 867 files, all additions, under docs/ (866) and the single run-owned `.kntnt-orchestrate/486.md` handoff. No existing test is weakened or removed. CONTRIBUTING.md is byte-identical to the base and drops or narrows no command. The product, Write, corpus, existing historical evaluation packets, source/support rules and aggregate record-index/changelog files are untouched. The handoff supplies the eventual record-index entry without editing a run-owned aggregate. There is no delivery-channel requirement in the authoritative issue thread and no implementation-role SHA to identify in a no-implementation result.

## Verifier evidence and cleanup

Evidence handoffs beside this verdict: `verifier-gate-complete.json`, four `verifier-gate-*.log` files, `verifier-gate-commands.json`, `verifier-gate-runner.py` (the exact runner recipe), `verifier-native-artifact-audit.json`, `verifier-scope-freeze-audit.json`, process/runtime registration receipts, process-completion receipt, load-context receipt and cleanup receipt. These are deliverables and are retained.

The sole removable verifier runtime path is `/private/tmp/kntnt-orchestrate-20261002.o7bmMK/ticket-486-scratch/verifier-runtime`. It is removed by a literal full-path command without force flags after the owned process group is proved empty. The final receipt records absence, unchanged head and clean tree. No verifier process or waiter is left running.

**Final verdict: FAIL. Criterion 1's explicit no-ticket blind-path requirement is unmet; the otherwise green project gate and verified target non-reproduction do not make that requirement optional.**
